title: CAGE: A FRAMEWORK FOR CULTURALLY ADAPTIVE RED-TEAMING BENCHMARK GENERATION
measurement_description: The paper measures the vulnerability of large language models to generating harmful content, specifically bias and hate speech, related to religion. This is evaluated within a red-teaming framework where prompts targeting religious stereotypes or discriminatory content are used to test model safety alignments.
findings: Under the 'Bias and Hate' category, prompts related to 'Religion' showed moderate-to-high Attack Success Rates (ASR) (≥ 0.6) depending on the model, indicating a significant vulnerability to generating harmful religious content. The AutoDAN attack method revealed particularly high ASR for models like Llama, Qwen, and Gemma in the religion sub-category.
